de.help_peak_slot: Jede Viertelstunde hat ein Energiebudget (Ihr Zielwert für 15 Minuten). SEM verfolgt, was dieses Fenster bereits bezogen hat, und begrenzt jeden Befehl so, dass das Fenster den Zielwert einhält.
de.config_proposed_help: SEM hat diese nicht überprüft — sie stammen daraus, was diese Integration laut eigener Angabe anlegt. Übernimm die, die stimmen; ändern kannst du sie später jederzeit mit den Auswahlfeldern unten. Und sag uns Bescheid: so wird aus einer Vermutung unterstützte Hardware.
de.config_proposed_per_charger: beim Ladegerät setzen, unten unter EV-Ladegeräte
de.config_proposed_observe_only: ein Betriebsmodus — SEM liest ihn und schreibt ihn nie; du stellst ihn ein
de.config_proposed_not_loaded: die Entität steht in der Registry, aber Home Assistant hat sie nie erzeugt — kein Button, bis sie lädt
de.config_proposed_no_unit: diese Entität meldet keine Einheit; SEM braucht hier {wanted} und rät nicht
de.config_proposed_unit_mismatch: diese Entität meldet {seen}; SEM braucht hier {wanted}
de.config_proposed_options_unmapped: dieses Select hat keine Option namens {missing} — setze die vier Strategiewerte im Batterie-Abschnitt passend zu seinen Optionen: {options}
de.config_help_import_surcharge: Optionale Gebühr auf jede importierte kWh (Netznutzung + Energieabgabe). Nur wenn deine dynamische Preis-Entität sie nicht enthält. Keine Grundgebühr; kein Einfluss auf die Einspeisung.
de.config_proposed_pair_incomplete: halbes Paar — dieses Gerät hat keinen {missing}-Sensor, und eine Hälfte allein läse sich wie ein Zähler, der nur bezieht
de.config_proposed_pair_blocked: halbes Paar — der {missing}-Sensor ist noch nicht nutzbar, und eine Hälfte allein läse die andere Richtung als 0 W
de.config_help_hp_contact_values: Dieser Kontakt ist eine Text-/Zahlen-/Auswahl-Entität, kein Schalter — SEM braucht daher für jede Stellung den exakten Wert, den es schreiben muss (das eigene Vokabular der Integration; EMS-ESP überträgt SG-Ready z. B. als Bitfolge). Beide Werte sind erforderlich.
de.config_help_export_guard: Bei negativem Einspeisepreis begrenzt SEM die Einspeisung am Wechselrichter auf null — nachdem Batterie, Auto und Lasten an der Reihe waren. Standardmäßig aus.
de.config_help_export_guard_override: Den Wächter auch dann handeln lassen, wenn der Wechselrichter einen Fahrplan des Netzbetreibers meldet (Huawei DI-Steuerung). Nur einschalten, wenn der Betreiber das erlaubt.
de.config_help_battery_house_sink: Den Speicher durch günstige Stunden halten und in teuren Stunden für das Haus ausgeben. Standardmäßig aus.
de.config_help_ev_morning_window: Vor der eingestellten Abfahrt den Speicher bis zur Untergrenze ins Auto entladen — nur wenn die heutige Prognose ihn wieder füllt. Standardmäßig aus.
de.config_help_export_guard_engage_s: Wie lange der Preis negativ bleiben muss, bevor die Begrenzung greift — Preise kreuzen die Null oft; der Wechselrichter darf nicht flattern.
de.config_help_export_guard_release_s: Wie lange der Preis positiv bleiben muss, bevor die Begrenzung aufgehoben wird.
de.config_help_ev_morning_window_hours: Stunden vor der Abfahrt, ab denen das Fenster geöffnet ist.
de.config_help_battery_morning_drain_floor_: Das Fenster entlädt den Speicher nie unter diesen SOC.
de.config_help_house_power_sensor: Ihr Wechselrichter liefert den Hausverbrauch eventuell direkt (z. B. Fronius SolarNet „Leistung Verbrauch“). SEM rechnet seinen eigenen Wert aus Solar, Netz, Batterie und EV aus, und bei einem Hybrid steckt in dieser Summe auch der Wandlungsverlust — 30 bis 60 W bei einem Fronius GEN24. Ist hier ein Sensor gewählt, zeigt SEM beide Zahlen und ihren Unterschied. Der eigene Wert von SEM bleibt gleich, also ändert sich auch keine seiner Entscheidungen.
de.config_help_setpoint_model: Wie SEMs Watt die Entität erreichen. signed (Standard): + Entladen, − Laden. inverted: gespiegelt, z. B. Victrons ESS-Netzsollwert. direction_select: ein Laden/Entladen-Select plus eine vorzeichenlose Watt-Zahl, z. B. Anker Solix.
de.config_help_direction_entity: Das Select, das die Richtung des Batteriestroms bestimmt. SEM setzt es vor dem Schreiben der Watt-Zahl und wartet, bis es zurückgelesen wird.
de.config_help_direction_values: Die Optionstexte Ihres Richtungs-Selects. Standard sind die von Anker (discharge / charge).
de.pause_charging_hint: Stellt diese Ladestation für die gewählte Zeit auf Aus und danach wieder auf ihren Modus. Ein gewählter Modus beendet die Pause vorzeitig.
de.pause_resume_hint: Einen Modus wählen, um sofort fortzusetzen.
de.hint_msg_night_load: Das Haus hat die ganze Nacht {watts} W gebraucht, sonst {usual} W.
de.hint_msg_grid_rise: Netzbezug heute {kwh} kWh (sonst {usual}) bei gleicher Sonne.
de.hint_msg_cheap_now: Strom ist jetzt günstig. {cars}: steckt und lädt nicht.
de.hint_msg_weekly_summary: Diese Woche: {solar} kWh Solar · {self_use} % Eigenverbrauch · {grid} kWh aus dem Netz · {ev} kWh ins Auto · {cost:.2f} {currency}.
de.config_help_hints: Kurze Meldungen, wenn etwas nicht stimmt. Aus: keine. Wochennotiz: nur die Sonntagsübersicht. Alle Hinweise: ein Sensor sendet nicht, eine schwere Nacht, steigender Netzbezug, günstiger Strom bei wartendem Auto, und die Wochennotiz.
de.ev_dep_tap_hint: Tag antippen für eine eigene Zeit, leeren für {time}
de.ev_dep_late_hint_plan: {span} · ≈ {kwh} kWh · ca. {cost} — läuft unabhängig vom Preis
de.ev_dep_help_days: „Fertig bis“ ist die Abfahrt an den meisten Tagen. Tippe einen Tag an, um ihm eine eigene Zeit zu geben; der umrandete Tag ist die Abfahrt, auf die der Plan heute Nacht hinarbeitet.
de.ev_dep_help_one_block: Ein durchgehender Ladevorgang im günstigsten Abschnitt der Nacht statt der günstigsten Einzelstücke. Passt der heutige Bedarf in keinen einzelnen Abschnitt, sagt der Plan das und lädt in Stücken.
de.ev_dep_help_late: Die letzten Minuten vor der Abfahrt laden unabhängig vom Preis, und der Rest der Nacht endet, bevor sie beginnen. Der Plan bucht sie mit der Leistung, die das Netzlimit dort zulässt.
de.ev_boost_hint: Die Hausbatterie in dieses Auto, nur für diese Ladung. Hausbatterie {soc} % → etwa {kwh} kWh für das Auto.
de.ev_boost_ends: Endet, wenn das Auto abgesteckt wird, der Modus wechselt oder die Batterie {floor} % erreicht. Ein Neustart beendet ihn ebenfalls.
de.ev_boost_not_permitted: Die Batterie darf dieses Auto nicht speisen: ihre Freigabe ist aus.
de.ev_boost_end_permission_off: die Freigabe der Batterie wurde ausgeschaltet
de.ev_boost_help: Einmalig: Die Hausbatterie speist dieses Auto bis zur gewählten Untergrenze. Der Boost endet, wenn das Auto abgesteckt wird, der Modus wechselt, die Batterie die Untergrenze erreicht oder ihre Freigabe ausgeschaltet wird — auch ein Neustart beendet ihn. Die dauerhafte Freigabe bleibt unverändert.
de.plan_ev_charge_late: Nachladen vor der Abfahrt — läuft unabhängig vom Preis
de.load_phase_tooltip: Die Phase, an der diese Last hängt. Liegt eine Phase über ihrem Limit, schaltet SEM zuerst die Lasten dieser Phase und dreiphasige Lasten ab, Lasten mit unbekannter Phase erst danach.
de.load_phase_measured_hint: aus dem eigenen Strom der Ladestation gemessen
de.config_help_shed_signal_entity: Der Kontakt, den Ihr Netzbetreiber schaltet. Leer lassen, wenn Sie keinen haben.
de.config_help_shed_signal_limit: Solange das Relais an ist, hält SEM den Netzbezug des Hauses unter diesem Limit. Solarstrom zusätzlich ist erlaubt.
de.cfg_help_behind_operator_relay: Der Netzbetreiber schaltet dieses Gerät ab. SEM plant es nicht, solange das Relais an ist.
de.operator_limit_banner: Netzbetreiber: Limit {kw} kW seit {time} — Solarstrom zusätzlich ist erlaubt
de.config_role_legend_lead: SEM liest dieses Ladegerät von seinem Gerät.
de.hint_msg_weekly_co2: Ihr Solarstrom hat diese Woche {co2} kg CO₂ vermieden.
de.config_help_grid_co2_entity: Wird über die Einheit gefunden (g oder kg CO₂ pro kWh). Wähle nur einen, wenn SEM den falschen fand.
de.config_help_outdoor_temperature_entity: Wird über den Namen gefunden, sonst Ihre Wetter-Entität. Nur wählen, wenn SEM das falsche gewählt hat.
de.config_help_simulation_tab: Zeigt den Simulations-Tab. Markiert dazu jeden Tag und liest einmal die letzten 90 Tage. Standardmäßig aus.
de.simulation_sub: Spielt Ihre gespeicherten Tage mit SEM nach. Ergebnisse nach einer geänderten Entscheidung sind geschätzt, nicht gemessen.
de.sim_sub: Spielt deine aufgezeichneten Tage durch SEM ab. Ergebnisse nach einer geänderten Entscheidung sind geschätzt, nicht gemessen.
de.sim_no_days: Noch keine aufgezeichneten Tage. SEM markiert jeden Tag nach Mitternacht.
de.sim_cancelled: Gestoppt. Das sind die Tage, die gelaufen sind.
de.sim_est_legend: = geschätzt. Nach einer geänderten Entscheidung werden die Flüsse aus der Energiebilanz berechnet, nicht gemessen. Grün = günstiger, Orange = teurer.
de.sim_limits: Stundenmittel: kurze Preis- und Lastspitzen werden geglättet. Auto und andere Verbraucher bleiben wie aufgezeichnet.
de.sim_cant_simulate: Dieser Zeitraum lässt sich nicht verlässlich simulieren: Ihre eigenen Einstellungen liegen {pct} % daneben.
de.sim_ev_moved: Auto: {moved} kWh verschoben, {short} kWh nicht geliefert
de.sim_period_note: Der ganze Zeitraum läuft als eine Kette: Die Batterie nimmt ihre Ladung von Tag zu Tag mit. Eine Lücke von bis zu zwei Tagen wird überbrückt; eine längere beginnt wieder beim aufgezeichneten Stand.
de.sim_filter_hint: Tippe auf eine Tagesart, um nur diese Tage zu zeigen. Tippe auf einen Tag für die Details.
de.sim_stored_sum: Zusätzliche Energie in der Batterie am Ende der Abschnitte, aufsummiert: {kwh} kWh = {value}
de.sim_day_net: Inkl. was die Batterie gewonnen hat: {d}
de.sim_repriced_note: * Ist-Wert zu Ihren gesetzten Preisen neu bewertet, nicht zu den bezahlten.
de.sim_days_checked: Einstellungsprüfung: {n} Tage genutzt, {m} ausgelassen (ein Zähler sprang).
de.sim_car_error: Tage mit Auto: Ihre Einstellungen weichen um {pct} % ab (über {n} Tage).
de.sim_net_ev_note: Die Netto-Summe zählt auch {kwh} kWh, die das Auto nicht bekam ({value}).
de.config_help_value_preset: Füllt die Felder unten. 'Keine' fügt nichts hinzu: die Preise bleiben, wie sie sind. 'Niederlande ab 2027' setzt Energiesteuer und 21 % MwSt.; Aufschlag und Gebühr Ihres Lieferanten tragen Sie selbst ein.
de.config_help_price_basis: Alles inklusive: Steuer und MwSt. sind schon im Preis (Tibber, Preis von der Rechnung) — nichts wird addiert. Spotpreis inkl. MwSt.: Steuer und Aufschlag werden mit MwSt. addiert. Spotpreis: Steuer, Aufschlag und MwSt. werden addiert.
de.config_help_import_markup: Was Ihr Lieferant pro bezogener kWh aufschlägt, ohne MwSt.
de.config_help_import_energy_tax: Energiesteuer pro bezogener kWh, ohne MwSt.
de.config_help_import_vat_percent: MwSt. auf die bezogene kWh, in Prozent.
de.config_help_fee_model: Was Ihr Lieferant für eingespeisten Strom verlangt: pro kWh, in Stufen nach kWh dieses Jahr oder ein fester Betrag pro Monat.
de.config_help_feed_in_fee: Pro kWh: die Gebühr pro kWh. Fest pro Monat: der Betrag pro Monat.
de.config_help_feed_in_fee_tiers: Nur für Stufen. kWh eingespeist dieses Jahr : Gebühr pro kWh, zum Beispiel 0:0, 1000:0.02, 3000:0.05
de.config_value_needs_spot_basis: Nur bei einem Spotpreis. Ein Endpreis enthält sie schon.
de.config_help_export_value_threshold: Ist eine verkaufte kWh weniger wert, stoppt SEM die Einspeisung: Batterie und Verbraucher nehmen zuerst die Sonne. 0 = nur unter null. Braucht den Schalter Einspeise-Wächter.
de.pacing_closed_meter: Einspeisung zu, Batterie nimmt die Sonne
de.device_tariff_hint: Nur für ein Gerät mit eigenem Zähler und Preis. Leer = Haustarif.
de.config_help_hp_tariff_rate: Fester Preis für den eigenen Zähler der Wärmepumpe, z. B. ein Wärmepumpentarif. 0 = Haustarif.
de.config_help_hp_tariff_entity: Ein Sensor mit dem Preis der Wärmepumpe, falls er sich ändert. Günstige Stunden folgen dann diesem Preis.
de.config_help_hp_tariff_meter: Optional. Der kWh-Zähler des eigenen Zählers der Wärmepumpe. Leer = SEM schätzt den Netzanteil.
de.why_empty: Noch keine Änderungen. SEM schreibt eine Zeile, sobald es ein Gerät ändert.
de.why_reason_charger_off: Du hast diese Ladestation auf Aus gestellt, SEM greift nicht ein.
de.why_reason_charger_full: Das Auto hat sein Ladeziel erreicht, das Laden endet.
de.why_reason_charger_max: Du hast volle Leistung gewählt, das Auto lädt so schnell es kann.
de.why_reason_charger_low_sun: Es gibt nicht genug Sonnenüberschuss, um das Auto zu laden.
de.why_reason_charger_sun_battery: Das Auto lädt mit Sonnenüberschuss und Hilfe der Hausbatterie.
de.why_reason_charger_battery_first: Die Hausbatterie ist fast leer, darum lädt sie vor dem Auto.
de.why_reason_charger_min_today: Das Auto braucht seine Mindestladung und die Nacht reicht nicht, darum lädt es jetzt.
de.why_reason_charger_min_done: Das Auto hat seine Mindestladung, das Laden endet.
de.why_reason_charger_plan_wait: Das Auto wartet auf die geplante Ladezeit.
de.why_reason_charger_plan_wait_until: Das Auto wartet auf die geplante Ladezeit um {time}.
de.why_reason_charger_deadline: Das Auto muss rechtzeitig fertig sein, darum lädt es jetzt.
de.why_reason_charger_top_up: Das Auto lädt aus dem Netz bis zu seiner Mindestladung.
de.why_reason_charger_peak_pause: Das Haus ist nahe an seinem Leistungslimit, das Auto pausiert.
de.why_reason_charger_peak_slow: Das Haus ist nahe an seinem Leistungslimit, das Auto lädt langsamer.
de.why_reason_charger_peak_stop: Das Haus ist über seinem Leistungslimit, das Auto stoppt zuerst.
de.why_reason_charger_phase_slow: Eine Phase ist nahe an ihrem Limit, das Auto lädt langsamer.
de.why_reason_charger_phase_stop: Eine Phase ist über ihrem Limit, das Auto stoppt.
de.why_reason_charger_inputs_missing: Einige Messwerte fehlen, das Auto lädt gleich schnell weiter.
de.why_reason_charger_car_declined: Das Auto hat das Laden nicht begonnen, SEM wartet vor dem nächsten Versuch.
de.why_reason_charger_wait_steady: SEM wartet, bis der Sonnenüberschuss lange genug anhält.
de.why_reason_charger_dip_hold: Die Sonne ist kurz eingebrochen, das Auto lädt langsamer, bevor es stoppt.
de.why_reason_charger_dip_stop: Die Sonne blieb zu schwach, das Auto hört auf zu laden.
de.why_reason_charger_phase_switch: SEM ändert die Zahl der Phasen, das Laden stoppt kurz.
de.why_reason_charger_grid_event: Dein Energieversorger hat um eine Pause gebeten, das Auto stoppt vorerst.
de.why_reason_charger_plan_override_stop: Du hast dieses Ladegerät bis {time} pausiert.
de.why_reason_charger_plan_override_run: Du hast bis {time} festgelegt, wie dieses Ladegerät lädt.
de.why_reason_battery_off: Du hast diese Batterie auf Aus gestellt, SEM greift nicht ein.
de.why_reason_battery_manual_sell: Du hast Verkaufen gewählt, die Batterie speist ins Netz ein.
de.why_reason_battery_manual_sell_hold: Du hast Verkaufen gewählt, aber der Ladestand ist zu tief oder unbekannt, darum wartet sie.
de.why_reason_battery_manual_charge: Du hast Laden gewählt, die Batterie lädt voll.
de.why_reason_battery_negative_price: Netzstrom hat einen negativen Preis, darum lädt die Batterie jetzt.
de.why_reason_battery_plan_charge: Der Plan lädt die Batterie jetzt aus dem Netz.
de.why_reason_battery_plan_wait: Die geplante Ladezeit hat noch nicht begonnen, die Batterie wartet.
de.why_reason_battery_plan_none: Der Plan sieht jetzt kein Laden aus dem Netz vor.
de.why_reason_battery_sell: Verkaufen lohnt sich jetzt, die Batterie speist ins Netz ein.
de.why_reason_battery_sell_forecast: Die Sonne füllt die Batterie wieder, darum verkauft sie, was die Nacht nicht braucht.
de.why_reason_battery_sell_hold: Die Nacht braucht den ganzen Speicher, darum verkauft die Batterie nichts.
de.why_reason_battery_sell_stop: Verkaufen lohnt sich nicht mehr, die Batterie hört auf zu verkaufen.
de.why_reason_battery_charge_stop: Die Batterie braucht jetzt keinen Netzstrom, sie hört auf, aus dem Netz zu laden.
de.why_reason_battery_feeds_car: Du hast es erlaubt, die Batterie darf das Auto laden, bis sie bei {floor}% ist.
de.why_reason_battery_house_held: Netzstrom ist gerade günstig, das Haus nutzt ihn und die Batterie spart ihre Ladung.
de.why_reason_battery_house_held_peak: Netzstrom ist günstig, aber das Haus ist nahe am Leistungslimit, darum hilft die Batterie.
de.why_reason_battery_house_blind: SEM kann das Haus gerade nicht messen, die Batterie versorgt es wie üblich.
de.why_reason_battery_car_not_allowed: Ein Auto ist angesteckt. Diese Batterie darf es nicht laden, darum versorgt sie nur das Haus.
de.why_reason_battery_car_level_unknown: Ein Auto ist angesteckt. Der Ladestand ist unbekannt, darum versorgt die Batterie nur das Haus.
de.why_reason_battery_car_below_floor: Ein Auto ist angesteckt. Die Batterie liegt unter den {floor}%, die die Nacht braucht, darum versorgt sie nur das Haus.
de.why_reason_battery_car_below_reserve: Ein Auto ist angesteckt. Die Batterie liegt unter ihrer Reserve, darum versorgt sie nur das Haus.
de.why_reason_battery_car_low_sun: Ein Auto ist angesteckt. Es gibt nicht genug Sonne, darum versorgt die Batterie nur das Haus.
de.why_reason_battery_car_shared: Ein Auto darf die Batterie nicht nutzen, darum versorgt sie nur das Haus und die anderen Autos.
de.why_reason_battery_grid_loads: Einige Geräte laufen mit günstigem Netzstrom, die Batterie versorgt sie nicht.
de.why_reason_battery_normal: SEM setzt gerade kein Limit, die Batterie lädt und entlädt von selbst.
de.why_reason_battery_end_charge: SEM beendet ein Laden aus dem Netz, das es vorher gestartet hat.
de.why_reason_battery_end_sell: SEM beendet einen Verkauf ins Netz, den es vorher gestartet hat.
de.why_reason_battery_charge_no_room: Das Haus ist nahe am Leistungslimit, die Batterie hört auf, aus dem Netz zu laden.
de.why_reason_battery_charge_slowed: Das Haus ist nahe am Leistungslimit, die Batterie lädt langsamer.
de.why_reason_solar: Es gibt genug Sonnenüberschuss, darum läuft es.
de.why_reason_tier1_battery: Sonnenüberschuss und etwas Batteriestrom betreiben es.
de.why_reason_tier2_battery: Es braucht noch Laufzeit, darum betreibt die Batterie es über Nacht.
de.why_reason_cheap_grid: Netzstrom ist gerade günstig, darum läuft es mit Netzstrom.
de.why_reason_surplus_short: Es gibt nicht genug Sonnenüberschuss, darum schaltet es aus.
de.why_reason_teardown: SEM fährt herunter und schaltet aus, was es gestartet hat.
de.why_reason_overnight_end: Der günstige oder nächtliche Lauf ist vorbei, darum schaltet es aus.
de.why_reason_target_met: Es lief heute lange genug, darum schaltet es aus.
de.why_reason_dependency: Das Gerät, von dem es abhängt, hat gestoppt, darum schaltet es auch aus.
de.why_reason_phase_guard: Eine Phase ist über ihrem Limit, darum schaltet es aus.
de.why_reason_phase_shed: Eine Phase ist über ihrem Limit, darum schaltet es aus.
de.why_reason_peak_shed: Das Haus ist über seinem Leistungslimit, darum schaltet es aus.
de.why_reason_peak_restore: Das Haus ist wieder unter seinem Leistungslimit, darum schaltet es wieder ein.
de.why_reason_deadline: Seine Frist ist nah, darum läuft es jetzt.
de.why_reason_plan_window: Der Plan lässt es jetzt laufen.
de.why_reason_vacation: Du bist weg, darum pausiert die Komfortheizung.
de.why_reason_mode_off: Du hast es auf Aus gestellt, darum beendet SEM den Lauf, den es gestartet hat.
de.why_reason_plan_closed: Die geplante Zeit ist vorbei, darum schaltet es aus.
de.why_reason_daily_max: Es hat seine längste Laufzeit für heute erreicht, darum schaltet es aus.
de.why_reason_stop_condition: Seine Stopp-Bedingung ist erfüllt, darum schaltet es aus.
de.why_reason_plan_wait: Es wartet auf die geplante Zeit.
de.why_reason_no_source: Es gibt keinen Sonnenüberschuss und keinen günstigen Strom, darum schaltet es aus.
de.why_reason_charger_stop_now: Die Leistung kommt so bald nicht zurück, darum stoppt das Auto jetzt.
de.why_reason_charger_ramp: SEM bringt den Strom in kleinen Schritten auf den neuen Wert.
de.why_reason_charger_hold_steady: SEM hält den Strom ruhig, um viele kleine Änderungen zu vermeiden.
de.why_reason_export_negative_price: Einspeisen kostet gerade Geld, darum stoppt SEM die Einspeisung ins Netz.
de.why_reason_export_not_worth: Einspeisen bringt {value} pro kWh, weniger als dein Limit von {threshold}, darum stoppt SEM die Einspeisung.
de.why_reason_export_released: Einspeisen lohnt sich wieder, darum hebt SEM das Einspeiselimit auf.
de.why_reason_export_guard_off: Du hast das Einspeiselimit ausgeschaltet, darum hebt SEM es auf.
de.why_reason_export_price_unknown: Der Einspeisepreis ist unbekannt, darum hebt SEM das Einspeiselimit auf.
de.config_help_batt_charge_end_entity: Wo der Wechselrichter selbst das Laden stoppt, in %. SEM liest ihn nur. Zwangsladen endet dort, wenn er unter 90 % liegt.
de.config_help_batt_charge_end_entity_each: Der eigene Ladeende-Stand dieser Batterie. Leer: SEM nutzt die Entität oben.
de.config_check_question: Passt das zu deinem Zähler oder deiner Energie-App? Wenn eine Richtung falsch ist, tippe unten.
de.config_check_wrong_sensor: Ein falscher Sensor? Wähle ihn in Alle Einstellungen.
de.cfg_in_use_hint: In Benutzung: {entity}. Dieses Formular überschreibt sie nur. Warmwasser und Wärmepumpe stellst du im Tab Konfiguration ein.
de.config_help_ext_ctrl: Für ein Gerät, das auch ein Versorger oder Netzbetreiber steuert. Ja, SEM hält sich zurück: Solange die Anzeige an ist, schreibt SEM nichts an das Gerät. SEM steuert, melde es mir: SEM behält die Kontrolle und zeigt eine Reparatur, wenn es Schreibzugriffe sieht, die nicht von SEM stammen. Die Anzeige ist ein Schalter, Binärsensor oder eine Auswahl, die zeigt, dass der Dritte die Kontrolle hat.

en.Germany (DVGW W 551): Storage ≥ 60°C, ci: Germany (DVGW W 551): Storage ≥ 60°C, circulation ≥ 55°C. Switzerland (SIA 385/1): Storage ≥ 60°C throughout tank. Austria (ÖNORM B 5019): 60°C storage, thermal disinfection at 70°C / 3 min. SEM forces a disinfection cycle if the tank hasn't reached the target temperature within the configured interval.
en.SEM is read-only — no device commands se: SEM is read-only — no device commands sent
en.Tariff windows · Night charging · Surplu: Tariff windows · Night charging · Surplus forecast
en.Waiting for first full charge detection: Waiting for first full charge detection
en.anti_cycle_hint: Stops rapid on/off cycling — protects pumps and relays. Blank keeps the default. A heat pump usually needs 10–20 minutes.
en.battery_may_export: Battery may sell to the grid
en.battery_mode_hint_auto: Auto: SEM charges from solar surplus, powers the house, and follows the schedule.
en.battery_mode_hint_force_charge: Charging to full now, regardless of price or surplus.
en.battery_mode_hint_force_discharge: Discharging to the grid now, down to the reserve SOC.
en.battery_mode_hint_off: SEM stays hands-off — the inverter manages this battery on its own.
en.battery_mode_hint_self_consumption: Charges from surplus and powers the house — never sells to the grid.
en.battery_overnight_help: Draw the home battery below the buffer (down to the reserve) to meet the minimum when there is no sun. Off by default.
en.battery_overnight_hint: Runs on solar surplus plus home-battery assist above the buffer; the daytime assist always applies in this mode.
en.battery_role_help: The battery charges from surplus the loads above it don't use. Drag it to change the order — loads above charge first, loads below yield. Below the reserve SOC the battery always charges first.
en.capacity_using_measured: SEM plans with this measured size, not the nameplate
en.capacity_using_nameplate: using the nameplate figure until enough nights are measured
en.charge_mode_hint_always_max_battery: Drains whenever total home demand exceeds solar, down to {buffer}% (buffer SOC). Protected below buffer.
en.charge_mode_hint_always_max_overnight: Charges at hardware max from grid + home battery.
en.charge_mode_hint_always_max_surplus: Charges at hardware max — solar is consumed first, then the home battery (per zones), then grid backfills the rest.
en.charge_mode_hint_min_plus_solar_battery: Drains for EV when home battery SOC ≥ {buffer}% (buffer). Below {buffer}% the home battery is protected from EV draw. Below {priority}% (priority floor) EV charging idles entirely.
en.charge_mode_hint_min_plus_solar_overnigh: Tops up at Min current until the Min target is reached.
en.charge_mode_hint_min_plus_solar_surplus: Guarantees the Min current using solar + battery + grid; rides surplus up to Max.
en.charge_mode_hint_solar_only_battery: Untouched — discharges only for the house, never for EV.
en.charge_mode_hint_solar_only_surplus: Only the solar surplus left over after the house. Never imports grid.
en.charge_mode_hint_solar_plus_cheap_batter: Untouched — discharges only for the house, never for EV.
en.charge_mode_hint_solar_plus_cheap_overni: Charges during the cheapest tariff hours only.
en.charge_mode_hint_solar_plus_cheap_surplu: Solar surplus only. Paused during expensive tariff windows.
en.charge_mode_battery_learning_info: Battery learner still gathering ({n}/{total} nights) — assists from live surplus now; forecast-led spending and the dynamic floor start once learning completes.
en.charge_mode_hint_solar_plus_battery_surp: Only the solar surplus left over after the house, topped up by the home battery. Never imports grid.
en.charge_mode_hint_solar_plus_battery_over: Idle — never grid-charges. Set an At-least floor for an overnight guarantee.
en.charge_mode_hint_solar_plus_battery_batt: Drains for EV when home battery SOC ≥ {buffer}% (buffer). Below {buffer}% the pack is protected from EV draw; below {priority}% EV charging idles entirely.
en.comfort_hint: Surplus banks comfort to the green mark; past the amber limit the unit runs from the sources you allow above.
en.comfort_example: Example: Keep at {keep}, extra {extra}. Surplus may heat up to {max}.
en.comfort_both_limits: The Solar Heating Target in the Configuration tab also applies. SEM stops at the lower of the two.
en.config_advanced_hint: Showing everything. Turn this off for just the essentials.
en.config_finetuning_folded: {n} sections for fine-tuning — show in All settings
en.config_everyday_nothing_here: Set up — nothing to change day to day.
en.config_battery_arbitrage_enable: Sell battery to grid on high export
en.config_battery_scheduler_intro: Forecast-driven overnight charging plans. Configure capacity, max charge power and roundtrip efficiency in HA settings — runtime targets adjust automatically once enabled.
en.config_detect_intro: What SEM found in your Home Assistant, with the evidence for every role. If a row is wrong, correct it with the pickers in the sections below — and please tell us: a near miss is a brand we almost support.
en.config_detect_offer: charger found — one click to add
en.config_detect_watch_only: charger found ({roles}) — no control SEM can drive
en.config_detect_watch_only_help: This charger only reports. SEM can read it but cannot start, stop or set its current. With one car integration that has its own charge control (charging amps and a charge switch), SEM offers this charger driven through the car.
en.config_detect_choose_vehicle_help: More than one car has its own charge control. SEM does not guess which one charges here: add this charger by hand with that car's charging amps and charge switch.
en.config_detect_prober_only: looks like a charger, no brand profile yet
en.config_detect_unmapped: on this device but no role
en.config_diagnose_clipboard_failed: Clipboard write failed — select the text manually.
en.config_ev_add_remove: Add / remove charger in HA settings
en.config_ev_add_via_settings: EV chargers are added via HA settings so SEM can register their entities. After adding one, return here to fine-tune.
en.config_forecast_install_hint: Install Forecast.Solar or Solcast in HA to enable forecast-aware planning.
en.config_forecast_spending_intro: Let SEM spend part of the battery tonight when tomorrow's sun is forecast to refill it. It measures your nights first and spends nothing until it has enough evidence. A charger in Solar + battery mode uses this budget on its own; this section governs what is sold to the grid.
en.config_heat_pump_intro: Pick the relays/climate entity that drive your heat pump. Changes save instantly — SEM will pick the heat pump up automatically.
en.config_heat_pump_manage: Heat pump entities in HA settings
en.config_help_arbitrage_min_export: Only sell battery energy to the grid when the export price is at least this much per kWh.
en.config_help_arbitrage_reserve_soc: Never discharge the battery to the grid below this SOC — your backup reserve.
en.config_help_batt_discharge_entity: The number entity SEM writes to cap battery discharge (e.g. the inverter's max-discharge-power).
en.config_help_batt_discharge_entity_each: This battery's own limit entity. Empty: SEM uses the entity above.
en.config_help_batt_max_discharge: The hard ceiling for ALL battery discharge (home + EV together) — written to the inverter's discharge-limit. The EV assist limit above is a sub-limit of this.
en.config_help_batt_protection: Limit battery discharge to the max power above to protect it and keep a reserve.
en.config_help_battery_arbitrage: When the dynamic export price is high enough to beat the cost of recharging later, discharge the battery to the grid to sell stored energy. Opt-in; never discharges below the reserve SOC.
en.config_help_battery_bidirectional: Enable if this battery's discharge-power entity is a bidirectional setpoint — one number entity for both charge and discharge, e.g. a Sessy. SEM then charges by writing a negative value to it. Leave off for a one-way forcible-discharge entity (e.g. Huawei).
en.config_help_battery_charge_pacing: Paces the daytime fill so the pack lands full at sunset instead of mid-morning — longer battery life, more midday sun captured. Needs the charge-power limit entity below and a settled forecast; below 35 % it always charges as fast as the sun allows.
en.config_help_battery_cycles_sensor: A hardware lifetime battery-cycle counter (e.g. from your Sonnen/Huawei integration). When set, SEM shows this instead of its throughput estimate. Autodetected on the battery device first.
en.config_help_battery_may_assist_ev: Allow tonight's budget to charge the car in the evening.
en.config_help_battery_may_export: Allow tonight's budget to be sold to the grid when the price is high.
en.config_help_battery_power_sensor: Live battery power (W, negative = discharge). Set this if battery power reads 0 while your Energy Dashboard has only battery energy. Autodetected first.
en.config_help_battery_soc_sensor: The sensor SEM reads for battery state-of-charge (%). Set this if SEM didn't auto-detect it — SOC is in your Energy Dashboard but shows as unavailable.
en.config_help_bs_block_mode: Pick the cheapest contiguous price window instead of scattered cheapest slots — slightly higher cost, less inverter start/stop cycling.
en.config_help_bs_capacity: Usable battery capacity in kWh — used to size pre-charge targets.
en.config_help_bs_cycle_cost: How much one stored kWh costs in battery wear. Set to 0 if you don't want SEM to penalise cycles.
en.config_help_bs_efficiency: Roundtrip storage efficiency (0.9 = lose 10% per charge/discharge cycle).
en.config_help_bs_enabled: When on, SEM pre-charges the battery overnight ahead of forecasted deficits.
en.config_help_bs_force_neg: When dynamic tariff goes negative, fill the battery even without a deficit.
en.config_help_bs_max_charge: Max battery charge power in W — caps overnight charging current.
en.config_help_bs_max_target_soc: Maximum SOC SEM will pre-charge to (leave headroom for solar in the morning).
en.config_help_bs_min_deficit: Minimum forecasted deficit before SEM bothers pre-charging at all.
en.config_help_bs_pessimism: How conservative SEM's forecast interpretation is. 0 = trust forecast; 1 = always assume worse.
en.config_help_bs_replan_interval: How often the rolling-horizon scheduler re-evaluates the night charge plan (picks up price updates and forecast changes).
en.config_help_bs_trigger_hour: Hour of day SEM starts planning the overnight pre-charge.
en.config_help_charge_power_limit_entity: Your inverter's max-charge-power number (Huawei: 'Maximum charging power'). SEM writes the paced cap here and restores your value when pacing ends.
en.config_help_cheap_price_threshold: At or below this price SEM treats electricity as cheap and will charge from the grid. Ignored on dynamic tariffs, which classify by percentile instead.
en.config_help_demand_charge_rate: Monthly per-kW demand charge from your DSO (the 15-min peak penalty).
en.config_help_deye_system_work_mode: Lets SEM switch your Deye to 'Selling First' when it decides to sell from the battery, and back afterwards. The inverter sets the rate.
en.config_help_deye_system_work_mode_entity: The select entity with Selling First / Zero Export To Load / Zero Export To CT. SEM suggests it when it finds one.
en.config_help_dynamic_feedin_entity: Optional sensor holding your live export (feed-in) price — e.g. your Tibber export-price sensor or a template like spot minus margin. When set, it overrides the flat Export rate so export revenue follows the market hour by hour.
en.config_help_tariff_schedule_entity: A Home Assistant Schedule helper. Its time blocks are the peak (HT) hours, priced at the Import rate; all other hours use the Off-peak rate.
en.config_help_dynamic_forecast_entity: Separate forecast sensor if your provider exposes it (Nordpool tomorrow, Octopus Agile next 24h).
en.config_help_dynamic_tariff_entity: A supported provider (Tibber, Nordpool, aWATTar, Amber, Octopus) or ANY entity whose state is the current price per kWh — e.g. your own template sensor. Expose a raw_today/raw_tomorrow curve attribute to unlock price levels and cheap-window planning (see setup guide: 'Bring your own price sensor').
en.config_help_ev_charge_mode: For go-e / Wattpilot boxes that latch after a stop: SEM stops and starts through this select instead of the current alone. Type the option labels exactly as your integration shows them — SEM never guesses them.
en.config_help_ev_charging_power: Live power draw of this charger. Used for surplus calculation + session tracking.
en.config_help_ev_connected_sensor: Sensor that goes on when an EV is physically plugged into this charger.
en.config_help_ev_current_control: The number entity SEM writes amperage to (or pair with a service in HA settings).
en.config_help_ev_daily_target: SEM tops up from the grid overnight so the car has at least this much by morning. A floor, not a limit. 0 = never use the grid.
en.config_help_ev_daily_target_max: Solar surplus stops charging here. Leave at full to charge freely from the sun.
en.config_help_ev_disable_delay: Deficit must persist this many seconds before a surplus charge stops; meanwhile the charger holds its minimum current. Protects the contactor from cloud-flicker on/off cycling.
en.config_help_ev_enable_delay: Solar surplus must persist this many seconds before a surplus charge starts. Prevents a single sun spike from closing the contactor.
en.config_help_ev_kwh_per_100km: Your car's real consumption. Used to turn a range figure into kWh — only matters if you set targets in km.
en.config_help_ev_phase_switch: The select/number/switch (helper entities too) that changes this wallbox between 1- and 3-phase charging (go-e psm, KEBA X-series, openWB). Named by you, never guessed. Setting it enables the Phases control on the EV card.
en.config_help_ev_phase_switching: Off by default while the 1/3-phase model is reworked — on some brands it paused chargers that never resumed. Turn on to test it on this charger; SEM then walks a safe stop → switch → settle → start sequence.
en.config_help_ev_phase_values: What to write for this position — a select's option name, a number's value, or on/off. Required for selects; number defaults to 1/3, switch to off/on.
en.config_help_ev_phases: How many phases this charger actually uses. Wrong here means every power calculation for it is wrong by the same factor.
en.config_help_ev_start_stop: Optional switch or button that physically starts/stops charging. Set this when 0 A alone does not release the charger (Smart EVSE, some OCPP boxes) — SEM then opens it instead of leaving the contactor cycling.
en.config_help_ev_target_soc: SEM stops treating the car as needing charge once it reaches this. A definition of "full", not a charging limit.
en.config_help_ev_target_soc_max: Solar surplus stops charging here. A ceiling, not a goal — leave at 100% to charge freely from the sun.
en.config_help_ev_target_type: kWh mode (default): SEM charges until your daily kWh target is reached. SOC mode: SEM charges until the vehicle SOC reaches your target — only available when a vehicle SOC sensor is configured above.
en.config_help_ev_vehicle_soc: Optional vehicle SOC sensor (Tronity / Bouncie / brand integration). Lets SEM stop at full.
en.config_help_expensive_price_threshold: At or above this price SEM avoids the grid and prefers the battery. Ignored on dynamic tariffs.
en.config_help_export_rate: Per-kWh credit you receive when exporting to the grid. For a dynamic/spot contract (e.g. Tibber) this is the spot price minus your provider margin — set a flat average here, or use the Feed-in entity below for live tracking. Leave it set so export revenue and ROI are calculated.
en.config_help_force_discharge_entity: The number entity that sets your inverter’s forcible battery-to-grid discharge power (e.g. the Huawei “Forcible discharge power”). Required for arbitrage to actuate.
en.config_help_forecast_spending: Selling to the grid needs this switch. The car does not: a charger set to Solar + battery may already spend the pack's forecast budget down to tonight's floor. Off means every number below is still measured and shown, but nothing is sold.
en.config_help_grid_export_entity: Optional override if SEM can't auto-pick the grid export sensor from your Energy Dashboard.
en.config_help_grid_import_entity: Optional override if SEM can't auto-pick the grid import sensor from your Energy Dashboard.
en.config_help_grid_power_sensor: Overrides the auto-detected grid power sensor. The import/export sign convention is detected automatically on the chosen sensor. Leave empty for auto (Energy Dashboard).
en.config_help_hp_boost_offset: How many °C above the user setpoint SEM lifts the climate target when surplus is available.
en.config_help_hp_climate: For climate-only setups (Nibe, Mitsubishi, Daikin): SEM raises the setpoint by boost-offset °C when surplus is available.
en.config_help_hp_energy_sensor: A cumulative energy counter (kWh) for the heat pump when it has no power sensor. SEM derives live power from it (or autodetects a power sensor first).
en.config_help_hp_invert_sg_ready: Enable for normally-closed (NC) relay wiring — inverts the SG-Ready contact logic.
en.config_help_hp_max_setpoint: Absolute ceiling for the climate setpoint — SEM won't push past this even with abundant surplus.
en.config_help_hp_power_sensor: Optional — lets SEM include heat-pump draw in load tracking and savings.
en.config_help_hp_priority: Lower = higher priority. EV usually gets 1-3; heat pump 4-6; pool 7-10.
en.config_help_hp_rated_power: The heat pump's rated electrical draw in watts, used for surplus sizing when there's no power sensor to calibrate from. Default 2000 W.
en.config_help_hp_relay: For SG-Ready setups: both contacts must be set. A contact is usually a switch; a text/number/select entity works too and asks for its two values. Skip if your heat pump only exposes a climate entity.
en.config_help_hp_temperature_sensor: The sensor SEM reads for the heat pump / buffer temperature.
en.config_help_hw_energy_sensor: A cumulative energy counter (kWh) for the hot water device when it has no power sensor. SEM derives live power from it (or autodetects a power sensor first).
en.config_help_hw_entity: A switch or water_heater entity SEM can toggle on/off to drive the boiler. Required.
en.config_help_hw_legionella_target: Target temperature for the periodic Legionella sterilisation cycle. Typically 60–65 °C.
en.config_help_hw_power_sensor: Optional — lets SEM include heat-pump draw in load tracking and savings.
en.config_help_hw_priority: Surplus-dispatch priority. Lower numbers are served first. 1 = highest priority.
en.config_help_hw_rated_power: The hot water device's rated electrical draw in watts, used for surplus sizing when there's no power sensor to calibrate from. Default 2500 W.
en.config_help_hw_solar_target: Solar-boost cutoff temperature. SEM stops activating the boiler on surplus when the water reaches this.
en.config_help_hw_temp_sensor: Optional. When configured, SEM blocks heating once the temperature reaches the active target. Leave empty to trust the boiler's internal thermostat only.
en.config_help_import_rate: Per-kWh price you pay when importing on the high-tariff side.
en.config_help_inverter_ac_limit: Maximum AC output in watts. Pacing opens its cap wherever solar would exceed this, so clipped sun is captured. 0 = not set.
en.config_help_lm_critical_protection: When on, devices marked critical are never shed (e.g. dialysis, server rack).
en.config_help_lm_emergency_peak: Hard kW ceiling. SEM forces every sheddable device off at this level.
en.config_help_lm_enabled: When on, SEM sheds non-critical loads to keep grid draw under the target peak.
en.config_help_lm_target_peak: Grid kW you want to stay under. SEM treats this as the soft ceiling.
en.config_help_lm_unlimited: Turns peak management off entirely — SEM stops sizing loads against the peak limit and never sheds to defend it. Only for connections no household load can threaten. Different from the switch above, which stops the shedding but keeps the limit as a sizing ceiling.
en.config_help_lm_warning_peak: kW at which SEM starts asking sheddable devices to reduce.
en.config_help_min_solar_power: Below this solar output (W), SEM stops surplus charging — even tiny PV is below the noise floor.
en.config_help_notif_charger: Push notifications for individual chargers (start, stop, target reached, etc.).
en.config_help_notif_mobile: Master switch — when off, SEM never sends mobile notifications regardless of service config.
en.config_help_notif_service: Which mobile_app service receives push notifications. Pick the device you want to be paged on.
en.config_help_observer_mode: Read-only mode: SEM watches your system but sends no commands. Safe to enable while learning the system.
en.config_help_off_peak_rate: Per-kWh price during the off-peak window (NT).
en.config_help_regulation_offset: A small power buffer kept as grid export so SEM doesn't risk importing while regulating surplus charging. The measured surplus is reduced by this amount before it's offered to devices. Default 50 W.
en.config_help_retention: SEM writes a lot of short-lived status rows — charging state, strategy, diagnostics. These carry no long-term statistics, so keeping them for weeks only grows your database. Pick how long to keep them. Your energy history is never affected: it lives in long-term statistics, which Home Assistant keeps forever.
en.config_help_retention_cleanup: Purge SEM's status history right now, using the retention above. Sensors that are charted — energy, power, anything with statistics — are never touched.
en.config_help_solar_forecast_source: Which forecast integration SEM reads. Auto prefers Solcast, then Forecast.Solar, then Open-Meteo — pick one if you run several side by side.
en.config_help_solar_production_sensor: Live solar power (W). Set this if your Energy Dashboard has only a solar energy (kWh) sensor, so Home consumption isn't stuck at 0. SEM tries to autodetect it first.
en.config_help_strategy_entity: The select entity that sets the battery's power strategy (e.g. select.sessy_*_power_strategy). SEM switches it to the API/active value while it drives the setpoint and restores your normal mode (nom/roi/eco) afterward. Needed for AC-coupled batteries like Sessy; leave empty otherwise.
en.config_help_strategy_values: The option string SEM writes to the power-strategy select for this mode. Defaults are Sessy's (api / eco / nom / idle) — map your own integration's option names here.
en.config_help_tariff_class_mode: Percentile adapts to your tariff's actual range; static uses your cheap/expensive thresholds verbatim.
en.config_help_tariff_mode: Static = one fixed price. Dynamic = pulls hourly prices from your tariff sensor. Calendar = scheduled HT/NT windows.
en.config_help_update_interval: Seconds between coordinator cycles. Lower = more responsive, higher = lighter on HA. 30 s is the sweet spot.
en.config_help_vacation_entity: Optional external vacation signal (e.g. your heat-pump app’s holiday mode, an input_boolean, or a calendar). While it is on, SEM suppresses comfort heating — same effect as the SEM Vacation mode switch; either source activates it.
en.config_help_vpp_direction_entity: Says whether the event asks you to draw more or less. Without it SEM cannot tell a curtailment from a boost.
en.config_help_vpp_enabled: Responds to grid operator (VPP) events, e.g. Axle Energy: exports battery power or pauses/boosts EV charging for the event window. Starts in observer mode — see docs/GRID_VPP.md for wiring and safety rails.
en.config_help_vpp_event_active_entity: Turns on while your grid operator has called an event. SEM follows it only when VPP support is enabled.
en.config_help_vpp_event_end_entity: When the current event finishes, so SEM can plan up to the edge of it rather than guessing.
en.config_help_vpp_observer: Dry run: SEM logs and notifies what it WOULD do during a VPP event but controls nothing. Turn off only after the log looks right.
en.config_help_vpp_pre_event_entity: Warns that an event is coming, letting SEM prepare — usually by charging before curtailment starts.
en.config_help_vpp_reserve_soc: Export events never discharge the home battery below this level.
en.config_hot_water_intro: Configure your hot-water boiler so SEM can boost it on solar surplus and run a periodic Legionella cycle.
en.config_notifications_intro: SEM sends push notifications via your mobile_app integration. Pick which events you want, and the recipient device, in HA settings.
en.config_overview_help: Everything below is editable in place. Open HA settings only if a section is missing the entity-picker you need.
en.config_pv_strings_help: Give each solar string a name (East, South, …). Leave a field blank to reset it to the default.
en.config_source_unavailable: override sensor unavailable — SEM keeps reading it (no silent fallback). Fix the sensor or clear the override.
en.config_sources_intro: Where SEM reads live power. Auto = derived from HA's Energy Dashboard. Override only when a detected sensor is wrong or unavailable.
en.config_tab_subtitle: Tune SEM without leaving the dashboard
en.config_tariff_manage: Tariff entity & mode in HA settings
en.config_tariff_mode_dynamic: Dynamic / price sensor (provider or any price entity)
en.control_verdict_help: Two things: whether SEM has a way to control this device at all, and whether it is allowed to right now.
en.cost_block_note: Avoided cost is money you did not spend — it is already reflected in the net cost above, so don't add the two together.
en.devices_auto_discovered:
Devices are auto-discovered from the HA Energy Dashboard.
Settings → Dashboards → Energy → Individual devices
en.drag_hint: Drag the ≡ handle or use ▲▼ arrows to reorder. Lower number = kept on longer.
en.energy_plan_active_note: Active — the plan's windows steer tonight's charging and loads.
en.energy_plan_arbitrage_tip: Advice only — would buying cheap energy into the battery and delivering it in an expensive hour pay after round-trip losses and wear? SEM does not act on this.
en.energy_plan_comfort_tip: Planned comfort banking: run in a free or cheap window to bank energy into the room before it drifts to its comfort limit. SEM never buys plain-rate power for this.
en.energy_plan_cov_yields: the plan could not fit it
en.energy_plan_fleet_partial: Partial battery data — plan uses only the reporting units
en.energy_plan_pending: Tonight's plan is computed when the night window opens
en.energy_plan_prices_final_tip: Tomorrow's day-ahead prices are published — the preview is priced with the real curve.
en.energy_plan_prices_preliminary_tip: Tomorrow's day-ahead prices are not published yet — the preview will firm up when they land (usually early afternoon).
en.energy_plan_provisional_tip: A provisional look at tomorrow: the known asks packed into tomorrow's expected windows, the battery seeded with the level today's plan predicts for the morning. The real plan stamps at the period boundary.
en.energy_plan_reactive_tip: The plan does not cover this device right now — the reactive layer decides
en.energy_plan_review_at_ceiling: uses the full {asked} kWh every night — it may need more
en.energy_plan_review_batt_clipped: drained {drained} kWh overnight — and clipped {clipped} h at full: more was spendable
en.energy_plan_review_batt_refilled: drained {drained} kWh overnight, full again by {full_at}
en.energy_plan_review_batt_short: drained {drained} kWh overnight — the promised refill never came
en.energy_plan_review_learning: still learning — {nights} clean nights so far
en.energy_plan_review_on_target: the ask matches what it uses
en.energy_plan_review_sc_beat: kept {actual}% of the solar, better than the planned {predicted}%
en.energy_plan_review_sc_met: kept {actual}% of the solar, as planned ({predicted}%)
en.energy_plan_review_sc_missed: kept {actual}% of the solar, {predicted}% was planned
en.energy_plan_review_took_less: usually needs about {suggested} kWh of the {asked} kWh asked
en.energy_plan_shadow_note: Shadow mode — SEM is not acting on this plan yet.
en.energy_plan_strip_omitted: Timeline omitted — this night is too large to chart here.
en.energy_plan_why_day_only: daytime only, does not run at night
en.energy_plan_why_no_runtime_need: no runtime left to make up
en.energy_plan_whyc_battery_unseen: no battery found, so none was planned
en.energy_plan_whyc_no_load_needs_night: no load needs a night run
en.energy_plan_yield_reason: {planned} of {needed} kWh placeable — the reactive layer keeps this floor
en.ev_tariff_hint: In the cheapest hours; grid top-up pauses when expensive
en.fix_battery_sign_help: Flips battery charge/discharge if it looks inverted and copies a ready-to-paste report to your clipboard. Paste it into a GitHub issue so we can improve auto-detection for your battery.
en.fix_grid_sign_help: Flips grid import/export if it looks inverted and copies a ready-to-paste report to your clipboard. Paste it into a GitHub issue so we can improve auto-detection for your meter.
en.forecast_compare_help: Each source's own figure, next to how well it has actually predicted your roof. Sources may be configured for different array sizes, so compare the accuracy rather than the kWh.
en.forecast_planes_summed: Summed across {n} planes of your roof.
en.goal_hint_no_target: Set a daily target below for the top-up to take effect.
en.heat_pump_not_configured: No heat pump configured — set relays (SG-Ready) or a climate entity (climate-only) in Settings → SEM → Heat Pump.
en.help_device_configure: set or correct the control entity (switch) SEM uses for this device — needed when auto-detection picked the wrong one or found none.
en.help_device_mode: who controls this device. Off: SEM only monitors and never switches it. Peak Only: your own automations run it — SEM only switches it off to protect the grid peak and restores it afterwards (catch the surplus in your automation via the "Surplus Available" sensor or the surplus event). Solar only: SEM switches it on when the solar surplus covers its rated power and off when the surplus is gone (min. 5 min on / 1 min off against flicker). Solar + battery: the same, plus home-battery assist above the buffer.
en.help_device_peak: the grid-import limit peak protection defends. When the 15-min average import approaches it, SEM sheds devices in priority order (highest number first) and restores them when the peak passes.
en.help_device_priority: the order devices get surplus and survive peak shedding. Lower number = gets surplus first and stays on longest; higher number = shed first when the peak limit is at risk. Drag the ≡ handle or use the ▲▼ arrows.
en.help_device_requires: chains devices: this device only switches on while the selected device is already running (e.g. a booster pump that needs the main pump).
en.help_device_target: give the device a daily goal: minimum runtime (dumb loads like a pool pump) and/or an energy amount (metered loads), optionally finished by a deadline. Top-up policy decides what happens when the sun alone won't get there: Solar only never uses grid power and accepts missing the target; Cheap hours completes it during cheap tariff windows; Always force-runs the device in time to meet the deadline. Max runtime is a safety cap; Stop when ends the day early once an external sensor (e.g. the car's SOC) reaches the value. Peak protection always outranks these targets.
en.help_mode_off: SEM only monitors — never switches it.
en.help_mode_peak_only: Your own automation runs it; SEM only sheds it on a grid peak, then restores it.
en.help_mode_surplus: SEM runs it on solar surplus — never imports from grid.
en.horizon_learning_effect: learning: {days} of {needed} days — a safety margin applies meanwhile
en.horizon_not_published: This provider does not publish this horizon — nothing to learn from
en.horizon_trusted_effect: measured — SEM spends against this accuracy, no extra margin
en.legionella_info_body: Germany (DVGW W 551): Storage ≥ 60°C, circulation ≥ 55°C. Switzerland (SIA 385/1): Storage ≥ 60°C throughout tank. Austria (ÖNORM B 5019): 60°C storage, thermal disinfection at 70°C / 3 min. SEM forces a disinfection cycle if the tank hasn't reached the target temperature within the configured interval.
en.mode_tooltip: Off = never touched. Peak only = shed during grid peaks. Solar only = runs on solar surplus. Solar + battery = solar surplus plus battery assist above the buffer.
en.no_source_hint: Your forecast provider does not publish this horizon.
en.notif_battery_full: Battery full ({soc:.0f}%) — surplus available for appliances or export.
en.notif_daily_summary: Today: {solar:.1f} kWh solar · {autarky:.0f}% autarky · Saved {savings:.2f} {currency} · Net cost {net_cost:.2f} {currency}
en.notif_ev_deadline_unreachable: {name} can't reach its target by {deadline} — {kwh:.1f} kWh still needed in {hours:.1f} h
en.notif_ev_estimate_resume: {name}: car reported {sensor:.0f}% — topping up to your {target:.0f}% target.
en.notif_ev_estimate_stop: {name}: stopped at ~{target:.0f}% (estimated) — car sensor is {age:.0f} min old (last: {sensor:.0f}%). SEM measured the delivered energy and stopped to protect your target.
en.notif_high_grid_import: High grid import: {power_w:.0f}W ({peak_pct:.0f}% of peak limit). Consider reducing loads.
en.notif_low_forecast: Low solar forecast tomorrow: {tomorrow_kwh:.1f} kWh. Consider charging EV tonight.
en.notif_phase_guard_observer_warning: Phase limit exceeded in Observer Mode at {location} ({reason}) — no action was taken.
en.notif_phase_guard_recovered: Phase guard restored and armed after fresh safe readings.
en.notif_phase_guard_recovered_observer: Phase readings returned to safe levels.
en.observer_mode_readonly: SEM is read-only — no device commands are being sent
en.onboarding_banner_body: The Configuration tab puts every setting one click away — no more digging through Settings → Devices & Services.
en.onboarding_banner_title: New: configure SEM from the dashboard
en.overnight_battery_hint: Drains the home battery (down to the reserve floor) to finish the target when there is no sun.
en.overnight_grid_hint: Tops up from the grid during your cheap-tariff window to finish the target. Needs a tariff/cheap window configured.
en.overnight_off_hint: Solar only — the load waits for sun and may miss its target on a dark day.
en.plan_ev_charge_joint: planned window — the joint plan's block
en.plan_ev_charge_estimate: estimate — the energy plan has not covered the car yet
en.plan_strip_help: Forecast of what this charger will do over the next {hours} hours: grey = idle, purple = waiting for a cheaper tariff hour, green = charging, teal = target reached. The thin line on top marks cheap (green) and expensive (pink) tariff windows.
en.rate_set_by_inverter: Discharge rate is set by the inverter in this mode
en.require_missing_body: For the full dashboard, install "{name}" via HACS → Frontend, then hard-refresh this page (Ctrl+Shift+R).
en.requires_tooltip: Only activates when the selected device is running
en.reset_sign_detection_help: Clears the learned grid/battery power sign and re-learns it. Use if import/export (or charge/discharge) appears inverted. Trigger it while the system is clearly exporting/importing for a clean re-learn.
en.setting_help_cheap_threshold: Below this rate the price is classified as 'cheap' — enables solar_plus_cheap night charging windows.
en.setting_help_expensive_threshold: Above this rate the price is 'expensive' — solar_plus_cheap pauses during these hours.
en.setting_help_priority_soc: Below this SOC, the home battery has absolute priority — no EV charging at all.
en.setting_help_resume_soc: Battery must reach this SOC for EV assist to resume after a stop.
en.sign_flipped: Sign flipped — clipboard blocked, copy the report from the logs
en.sign_flipped_copied: Sign flipped — report copied to clipboard
en.soc_confirms_next_update: car sensor {age} min old; confirms on next update
en.soc_estimated_hint: Estimated from delivered energy — no vehicle SOC sensor configured. The car’s own reading may differ.
en.solar_only_hint: Solar only — the battery stays reserved for the house.
en.state_night_waiting: Night mode - Waiting for charging window
en.state_tariff_waiting: Tariff mode - Waiting for cheap price
en.stop_condition_hint: Optional — end the run early when any sensor crosses a value (e.g. tank full, temperature reached).
en.tile_help_capacity: Battery pack size — drives SOC estimation and range calculations.
en.tile_help_consumption: Average consumption used to estimate driving range from SOC.
en.tile_help_max_amps: Wallbox ceiling — highest current SEM may command.
en.tile_help_min_amps: SEM-side floor — minimum current SEM ever commands.
en.tile_help_start_amps: Initial ramp current when a session starts (soft start).
en.tile_help_vehicle_min_amps: Per-car handshake floor — set higher if your car ignores 6 A offers.
en.tip_battery_full_desc: Battery at {soc:.0f}% with {remaining:.1f} kWh solar still expected. Start large appliances to avoid export.
en.tip_battery_full_title: Battery nearly full — use surplus now
en.tip_battery_offset_desc: Battery discharged {discharge:.1f} kWh but grid import was {import_kwh:.1f} kWh. Consider adjusting battery strategy to cover peak consumption hours.
en.tip_battery_offset_title: Battery could offset more grid import
en.tip_best_window_desc: Run dishwasher, washing machine, or dryer during {window} — expected {remaining:.1f} kWh solar surplus remaining today.
en.tip_charge_ev_tonight_title: Weak solar tomorrow — charge EV tonight
en.tip_cheap_price_desc: Electricity price is currently {level}. Good time to charge EV or run appliances from grid.
en.tip_ev_good_solar_desc: Solar forecast shows {remaining:.1f} kWh remaining today. Solar charging should cover your EV needs — consider deferring grid charging.
en.tip_ev_grid_desc: Only {solar_pct:.0f}% of EV charging is from solar. Shifting charging to 10:00-15:00 could significantly reduce grid usage.
en.tip_excellent_self_desc: Self-consumption at {rate:.0f}% — well optimized. Your system is efficiently using solar production.
en.tip_expensive_price_desc: Electricity price is {level}. Minimize grid import — use battery and defer non-essential loads.
en.tip_heat_pump_desc: With {export_pct:.0f}% export rate, an SG-Ready heat pump could use solar surplus for water/space heating.
en.tip_high_export_desc: {export_pct:.0f}% of solar is exported. Adding a hot water diverter would capture ~{capture:.1f} kWh/day.
en.tip_low_self_desc: Self-consumption at {rate:.0f}%. Consider shifting loads to midday or adding battery storage.
en.tip_low_solar_tomorrow_title: Low solar tomorrow — use surplus today
en.tip_low_tomorrow_desc: Tomorrow's forecast is only {tomorrow:.1f} kWh. Consider running appliances today while {remaining:.1f} kWh surplus is still available.
en.tip_low_tomorrow_title: Low solar tomorrow — use surplus today
en.tip_strong_tomorrow_desc: Tomorrow's forecast is {tomorrow:.1f} kWh. Consider deferring large appliances to tomorrow for free solar.
en.tip_weak_tomorrow_ev_desc: Tomorrow: only {tomorrow:.1f} kWh expected. Night charging recommended to ensure the EV is ready.
en.tip_weak_tomorrow_ev_title: Weak solar tomorrow — charge EV tonight
en.vacation_mode_help: While away, SEM pauses comfort heating (heat pump boost and hot water). Legionella protection catches up when you return.
en.zone_help_assist_max_power: How much the home battery may give the EV — a sub-limit inside the total discharge limit below. Applies only to battery-assist charging (SOC above the buffer, real solar past the Solar Gate).
en.zone_help_assist_min_surplus: Minimum real solar surplus before the home battery helps charge the EV — in any mode. Below this the battery is reserved for the house. 0 = battery supports the EV everywhere, including overnight.
en.zone_help_autostart: Above this SOC, the home battery automatically helps the EV in min_plus_solar daytime.
en.zone_help_buffer: Battery is protected from EV draw below this SOC; solar still recharges it normally.
en.zone_help_priority: Critical reserve. Below this, all solar goes to the battery and EV charging idles.
en.peak_power_unsupported: This forecast source does not publish a peak power value
en.rebuild_nights_hint: Reads your battery's own recorded history and reconstructs these nights now, instead of waiting for them to happen
en.enable_horizon_sensor: Your integration ships this forecast sensor disabled — enable it in Home Assistant and SEM will start learning this horizon
en.help_peak_15min_avg: The 15-minute rolling average of grid import — the number a demand tariff bills. It is not what the meter shows right now: a car that has been charging for six of the last fifteen minutes moves this figure only a little.
en.help_peak_slot: Each clock quarter-hour has an energy budget (your target for 15 minutes). SEM tracks what this slot has already imported and caps every command it issues so the slot still lands on target.
en.config_proposed_help: SEM has not verified these — they come from what this integration says it creates. Accept the ones that look right; you can change any of them later with the pickers below. And do tell us: that is what turns a guess into supported hardware.
en.config_proposed_per_charger: set this on the charger, in EV chargers below
en.config_proposed_observe_only: a policy selector — SEM reads it and never writes it; you set it
en.config_proposed_not_loaded: the entity is in the registry but Home Assistant never produced it — no button until it loads
en.config_proposed_no_unit: this entity reports no unit; SEM needs {wanted} here and will not guess
en.config_proposed_unit_mismatch: this entity reports {seen}; SEM needs {wanted} here
en.config_proposed_options_unmapped: this select has no option named {missing} — set the four strategy values in the battery section to match its options: {options}
en.config_help_import_surcharge: Optional fee added to every imported kWh (transfer + energy tax). Only when your dynamic price entity excludes it. No fixed subscription; does not affect export.
en.config_proposed_pair_incomplete: half of a split pair — this device has no {missing} sensor, and one half alone would read as a meter that only ever imports
en.config_proposed_pair_blocked: half of a split pair — SEM cannot use the {missing} sensor yet, and one half alone would read the other direction as 0 W
en.config_help_hp_contact_values: This contact is a text/number/select entity, not a switch, so SEM needs the exact value to write for each position — the integration's own vocabulary (EMS-ESP carries SG-Ready as a bit string). Both are required.
en.plan_export_reopens: Export price positive again — meter open
en.config_help_export_guard: While the export price is negative SEM caps feed-in at zero at the inverter — after the battery, the car and the loads had their turn. Off by default.
en.config_help_export_guard_override: Let the export guard act even while the inverter reports an operator's schedule (Huawei DI active scheduling). Off unless you know the operator allows it.
en.config_help_battery_house_sink: Keep the pack through cheap hours and spend it on the house in expensive ones. Off by default.
en.config_help_ev_morning_window: Before the configured departure, empty the pack into the car down to the drain floor — only when today's forecast refills it. Off by default.
en.config_help_export_guard_engage_s: How long the price must stay negative before the cut is applied — prices cross zero often; do not flap the inverter.
en.config_help_export_guard_release_s: How long the price must stay positive before the cut is released.
en.config_help_ev_morning_window_hours: Hours before departure the window opens.
en.config_help_battery_morning_drain_floor_: The window never takes the pack below this SOC.
en.config_help_house_power_sensor: Your inverter may publish the house load directly (Fronius SolarNet 'Leistung Verbrauch', for example). SEM works its own figure out from solar, grid, battery and EV, and on a hybrid that sum also carries the inverter's conversion losses — 30 to 60 W on a Fronius GEN24. Name a sensor here and SEM publishes both numbers and the difference between them. Its own figure is unchanged, so nothing it decides changes either.
en.config_help_setpoint_model: How SEM's watts reach the entity. signed (default): + discharge, − charge. inverted: the mirror, e.g. Victron's ESS grid setpoint. direction_select: a charge/discharge select plus an unsigned watt number, e.g. Anker Solix.
en.config_help_direction_entity: The select entity that says which way the battery moves power. SEM sets it before writing the watt number, and waits until it reads back.
en.config_help_direction_values: The option strings of your direction select. Defaults are Anker's (discharge / charge).
en.pause_charging_hint: Sets this charger to Off for the chosen time, then back to its mode. Picking a mode ends the pause early.
en.pause_resume_hint: Pick a mode to resume now.
en.hint_msg_night_load: The house used {watts} W all night, usually {usual} W.
en.hint_msg_grid_rise: Grid use rose to {kwh} kWh (usually {usual}) with the same sun.
en.hint_msg_cheap_now: Power is cheap now. {cars}: plugged in and not charging.
en.hint_msg_weekly_summary: This week: {solar} kWh solar · {self_use} % self-use · {grid} kWh from the grid · {ev} kWh into the car · {cost:.2f} {currency}.
en.config_help_hints: Short messages when something is off. Off: none. Weekly note: the Sunday summary only. All hints: a sensor that stops sending, a heavy night, rising grid use, cheap power with the car idle, and the weekly note.
en.ev_dep_tap_hint: tap a day for its own time, clear it for {time}
en.ev_dep_late_hint_plan: {span} · ≈ {kwh} kWh · est. {cost} — runs whatever the price
en.ev_dep_help_days: Charge by is the departure on most days. Tap a day to give it a time of its own; the outlined day is the departure tonight's plan works to.
en.ev_dep_help_one_block: One continuous run in the cheapest stretch of the night instead of the cheapest pieces. When no single stretch can hold tonight's need, the plan says so and charges in pieces.
en.ev_dep_help_late: The last minutes before the departure charge whatever the price, and the rest of the night ends before they start. The plan books them at the rate the grid limit allows there.
en.ev_boost_hint: The house battery into this car, this charge only. House battery {soc} % → about {kwh} kWh for the car.
en.ev_boost_ends: Ends when the car unplugs, the mode changes or the battery reaches {floor} %. A restart ends it too.
en.ev_boost_not_permitted: The battery may not feed this car: its permission is off.
en.ev_boost_end_permission_off: the battery's permission was switched off
en.ev_boost_help: A one-off: the house battery feeds this car down to the floor you pick. It ends when the car unplugs, the mode changes, the battery reaches the floor or its permission goes off, and a restart ends it too. The standing permission is not changed.
en.plan_ev_charge_late: top-up before leaving — runs whatever the price
en.load_phase_tooltip: The supply phase this load sits on. When a phase is over its limit, SEM switches off that phase's loads and three-phase loads first, loads on an unknown phase only after them.
en.load_phase_measured_hint: measured from the charger's own current
en.config_help_shed_signal_entity: The contact your grid operator switches. Leave empty if you have none.
en.config_shed_signal_limit: Grid limit while it is on
en.config_help_shed_signal_limit: While the relay is on, SEM keeps the house's grid draw under this limit. Solar on top is fine.
en.cfg_help_behind_operator_relay: The operator switches this device off. SEM will not plan it while the relay is on.
en.operator_limit_banner: Grid operator: limit {kw} kW since {time} — solar on top is fine
en.config_role_legend_lead: SEM reads this charger from its device.
en.hint_msg_weekly_co2: Your solar avoided {co2} kg of CO₂ this week.
en.config_help_grid_co2_entity: Found by its unit (g or kg CO₂ per kWh). Pick one only if SEM found the wrong one.
en.config_help_outdoor_temperature_entity: Found by its name, else your weather entity. Pick one only if SEM chose the wrong one.
en.config_help_simulation_tab: Shows the Simulation tab. It also tags each day and reads the last 90 days once. Off by default.
en.simulation_sub: Replays your recorded days through SEM. Results after a changed decision are estimated, not measured.
en.sim_sub: Replays your recorded days through SEM. Results after a changed decision are estimated, not measured.
en.sim_no_days: No recorded days yet. SEM tags each day after midnight.
en.sim_cancelled: Stopped. These are the days that ran.
en.sim_est_legend: = estimated. After a changed decision, the flows are computed from the energy balance, not measured. Green = cheaper, orange = dearer.
en.sim_limits: Hourly averages: short price swings and peaks are smoothed. The car and other loads stay as recorded.
en.sim_cant_simulate: Can't simulate this period reliably: your own settings are off by {pct} %.
en.sim_ev_moved: Car: {moved} kWh moved, {short} kWh not delivered
en.sim_period_note: The whole period runs as one chain: the battery carries its charge from day to day. A gap of up to two days is bridged; a longer one starts again from the recorded level.
en.sim_filter_hint: Tap a day type to show only those days. Tap a day for its details.
en.sim_stored_sum: Extra energy left in the battery at stretch ends, summed: {kwh} kWh = {value}
en.sim_months_helps: The what-if comes out cheaper in: {months}
en.sim_preset_pv_ask_kwp: How many kWp of solar more?
en.sim_repriced_note: * Actual is re-priced at the rates you set, not the rates you paid.
en.sim_days_checked: Settings check: {n} days used, {m} left out (a counter jumped).
en.sim_car_error: Days with a car: your settings are off by {pct} % over {n} days.
en.sim_net_ev_note: The net total also counts {kwh} kWh the car did not get ({value}).
en.config_help_value_preset: Fills the fields below. 'None' adds nothing: prices stay as they are. 'Netherlands from 2027' sets energy tax and 21 % VAT; enter your supplier's markup and fee yourself.
en.config_help_price_basis: All-in: the price already has tax and VAT (Tibber, a rate from your bill) — nothing is added. Spot incl. VAT: tax and markup are added with VAT. Spot: tax, markup and VAT are all added.
en.config_help_import_markup: What your supplier adds per bought kWh, excl. VAT.
en.config_help_import_energy_tax: Energy tax per bought kWh, excl. VAT.
en.config_help_import_vat_percent: VAT on the bought kWh, in percent.
en.config_help_fee_model: What your supplier charges for the energy you send to the grid: per kWh, in tiers by kWh sent this year, or a fixed amount per month.
en.config_help_feed_in_fee: Per kWh: the fee per kWh. Fixed monthly: the amount per month.
en.config_help_feed_in_fee_tiers: For tiers only. kWh sent this year : fee per kWh, for example 0:0, 1000:0.02, 3000:0.05
en.config_value_needs_spot_basis: Only for a spot price. An all-in price already holds these.
en.config_help_export_value_threshold: When a sold kWh is worth less than this, SEM stops exporting: the battery and loads take the sun first. 0 = only below zero. Needs the Export guard switch.
en.pacing_closed_meter: export closed, battery takes the sun
en.device_tariff_hint: Only for a device with its own meter and price. Empty = house tariff.
en.device_tariff_heat_pump: Set in the heat pump settings.
en.config_help_hp_tariff_rate: A fixed price for the heat pump's own meter, e.g. a heat pump tariff. 0 = house tariff.
en.config_help_hp_tariff_entity: A sensor with the heat pump's price, if it changes. Cheap hours then follow this price.
en.config_help_hp_tariff_meter: Optional. The kWh counter of the heat pump's own meter. Empty = SEM estimates its grid share.
en.why_empty: No changes yet. SEM adds a row each time it changes a device.
en.why_reason_charger_off: You set this charger to Off, so SEM leaves it alone.
en.why_reason_charger_full: The car reached its charge limit, so charging stops.
en.why_reason_charger_max: You chose full power, so the car charges as fast as it can.
en.why_reason_charger_low_sun: There is not enough spare sun to charge the car.
en.why_reason_charger_sun: The car charges with spare sun.
en.why_reason_charger_sun_battery: The car charges with spare sun and help from the house battery.
en.why_reason_charger_battery_first: The house battery is low, so it charges before the car.
en.why_reason_charger_min_today: The car needs its minimum charge and the night is too short, so it charges now.
en.why_reason_charger_min_done: The car has its minimum charge, so charging stops.
en.why_reason_charger_plan_wait: The car waits for the planned charging time.
en.why_reason_charger_plan_wait_until: The car waits for the planned charging time at {time}.
en.why_reason_charger_deadline: The car must be ready in time, so it charges now.
en.why_reason_charger_top_up: The car charges from the grid up to its minimum.
en.why_reason_charger_no_night: This mode does not charge at night.
en.why_reason_charger_peak_pause: The house is near its power limit, so the car pauses.
en.why_reason_charger_peak_slow: The house is near its power limit, so the car charges more slowly.
en.why_reason_charger_peak_stop: The house is over its power limit, so the car stops first.
en.why_reason_charger_phase_slow: One phase is near its limit, so the car charges more slowly.
en.why_reason_charger_phase_stop: One phase is over its limit, so the car stops.
en.why_reason_charger_inputs_missing: Some readings are missing, so the car keeps its current charging speed.
en.why_reason_charger_car_declined: The car did not start charging, so SEM waits before it tries again.
en.why_reason_charger_wait_steady: SEM waits until the spare sun lasts long enough to start.
en.why_reason_charger_dip_hold: The sun dropped for a moment, so the car slows down before it stops.
en.why_reason_charger_dip_stop: The sun stayed too low, so the car stops charging.
en.why_reason_charger_phase_switch: SEM changes how many phases the car uses, so charging stops for a moment.
en.why_reason_charger_grid_event: Your energy provider asked for a pause, so the car stops for now.
en.why_reason_charger_plan_override_run: You set how this charger charges until {time}.
en.why_reason_battery_off: You set this battery to Off, so SEM leaves it alone.
en.why_reason_battery_manual_sell: You chose to sell, so the battery sends power to the grid.
en.why_reason_battery_manual_sell_hold: You chose to sell, but the battery level is too low or unknown, so it waits.
en.why_reason_battery_manual_charge: You chose to charge, so the battery charges to full.
en.why_reason_battery_negative_price: Grid power has a negative price, so the battery charges now.
en.why_reason_battery_plan_charge: The plan charges the battery from the grid now.
en.why_reason_battery_plan_wait: The planned charging time has not started, so the battery waits.
en.why_reason_battery_plan_none: The plan has no grid charge for the battery now.
en.why_reason_battery_sell: Selling pays well now, so the battery sends power to the grid.
en.why_reason_battery_sell_forecast: The sun will refill the battery, so it sells what tonight does not need.
en.why_reason_battery_sell_hold: Tonight needs all the stored power, so the battery does not sell.
en.why_reason_battery_sell_stop: Selling no longer pays, so the battery stops selling.
en.why_reason_battery_charge_stop: The battery needs no grid power now, so it stops charging from the grid.
en.why_reason_battery_feeds_car: You allowed it, so the battery may charge the car until it is down to {floor}%.
en.why_reason_battery_house_held: Grid power is cheap now, so the house uses it and the battery keeps its power.
en.why_reason_battery_house_held_peak: Grid power is cheap, but the house is near its power limit, so the battery helps.
en.why_reason_battery_house_blind: SEM cannot measure the house now, so the battery powers it as usual.
en.why_reason_battery_car_not_allowed: A car is plugged in. This battery may not charge it, so it powers only the house.
en.why_reason_battery_car_level_unknown: A car is plugged in. The battery level is unknown, so it powers only the house.
en.why_reason_battery_car_below_floor: A car is plugged in. The battery is below the {floor}% tonight needs, so it powers only the house.
en.why_reason_battery_car_below_reserve: A car is plugged in. The battery is below its reserve, so it powers only the house.
en.why_reason_battery_car_low_sun: A car is plugged in. There is not enough sun, so the battery powers only the house.
en.why_reason_battery_car_shared: One car may not use the battery, so it powers only the house and the other cars.
en.why_reason_battery_grid_loads: Some devices run on cheap grid power, so the battery does not power them.
en.why_reason_battery_normal: SEM sets no limit now, so the battery charges and empties on its own.
en.why_reason_battery_end_charge: SEM ends a grid charge it started earlier.
en.why_reason_battery_end_sell: SEM ends a sale to the grid it started earlier.
en.why_reason_battery_charge_no_room: The house is near its power limit, so the battery stops charging from the grid.
en.why_reason_battery_charge_slowed: The house is near its power limit, so the battery charges more slowly.
en.why_reason_solar: There is enough spare sun, so it runs.
en.why_reason_tier1_battery: Spare sun and some battery power run it.
en.why_reason_tier2_battery: It still needs run time, so the battery runs it overnight.
en.why_reason_cheap_grid: Grid power is cheap now, so it runs on the grid.
en.why_reason_surplus_short: There is not enough spare sun, so it turns off.
en.why_reason_teardown: SEM is shutting down, so it turns off what it started.
en.why_reason_overnight_end: The cheap or overnight run is over, so it turns off.
en.why_reason_target_met: It ran long enough today, so it turns off.
en.why_reason_dependency: The device it depends on stopped, so it turns off too.
en.why_reason_phase_guard: One phase is over its limit, so it turns off.
